title: Dedicated throughput floor, crediting formulas, and escalation playbook
creator: Aisha Gupta
description:
Purpose: Define a concise, implementable specification for a Dedicated Capacity throughput guarantee that can be embedded in contracts and instrumented by the runtime and console. This ticket focuses on: 1) formal definitions (throughput floor, measured throughput, availability window), 2) a deterministic crediting formula tied to measurable metrics, 3) an error-budget model and burn rate windows, and 4) an operational escalation and remediation playbook including autoscale triggers and tenant-visible reports. Scope excludes pricing negotiation language and detailed legal indemnities — those will be handled by Sales/Legal after we align on measurable metrics and remediation steps.

Why this is needed: Customers buying Dedicated expect predictable per-second serving capacity for a committed price. Current contract drafts rely on vague language ("guaranteed throughput") and a variety of post-hoc interpretations. This causes disputes and inconsistent crediting. We need a single canonical definition the runtime can compute, the Console can display, and Legal can reference in a short contract clause.

Deliverables: 
- A human-readable spec (this ticket) with definitions and examples.
- Machine-friendly measurement guidance (metric names and query snippets for runtime telemetry).
- A crediting formula with worked examples and edge-case rules (partial window, scheduled maintenance, force majeure).
- An operational playbook: detection, autoscale policy interaction, customer notifications, credit issuance, and post-mortem requirements.

Key decisions to make in this ticket: 
- Whether the SLA uses a rolling-window percentile (p95/p99) or an availability-floor measured as average achieved throughput vs committed throughput over discrete billing windows. Recommended: a hybrid model: discrete billing windows for crediting (daily or weekly), with rolling percentiles for SLO monitoring.
- How autoscale events that change capacity affect the baseline commitment and credits. Recommended: credits measured against the "effective committed capacity" which is adjusted for planned capacity changes and successful autoscale increases within a defined slippage window.
- Tolerance for short spikes of degradation (transient network blips) before crediting triggers. Recommended: a short debounce (2 minutes) and a minimum impact threshold (>=5% shortfall for window to count).
acceptance_criteria: Spec text including definitions for throughput_floor, measured_throughput, credit_window, and exclusion_reasons
Crediting formula expressed in plain English and with two worked numeric examples (daily billing window and weekly billing window)
Metric names and sample PromQL/SQL queries that Console and Billing will use to compute credits
Operational playbook with step-by-step actions for detection, customer notification, escalation, credit issuance, and post-incident reporting
Sign-off from Runtime engineering, Console product, and Legal (recorded as comments/links)

proposed_clause_snippet: If Redwood fails to achieve the Committed Throughput (as defined below) for a given Billing Window due to Redwood-managed infrastructure or software defects (excluding Scheduled Maintenance and Force Majeure), Customer will be eligible to receive Service Credits equal to the Credit Amount computed per the Crediting Formula. Credits will be applied to the Customer's next invoice within two billing cycles.
measurement_guidance: Metric definitions: 1) dedicated.commitment_tokens_per_sec — the committed tokens/sec for the customer at each second; 2) dedicated.serve_tokens_per_sec — tokens successfully served to the customer per second; 3) dedicated.capacity_events — autoscale up/down events with timestamps and reason codes. Measurement window: the Billing Window is aligned to UTC-day (00:00:00 to 23:59:59) unless the customer and Sales agree on a different billing cadence. Compute measured_throughput = sum(serve_tokens_sec over window) / length(window). Credited_shortfall = max(0, (committed_throughput - measured_throughput) / committed_throughput).
crediting_formula_plain_english: For each Billing Window: 1) Determine effective_committed = committed_throughput adjusted for any Planned Capacity Reductions or agreed changes effective during the window. 2) Compute observed = average served tokens/sec during the Billing Window after applying debounce (ignore drops shorter than 2 minutes) and excluding windows where scheduled_maintenance_flag=true. 3) If observed < effective_committed and shortfall fraction > 5%, compute CreditFraction = min(ObservedShortfallFraction, 1.0). 4) CreditAmount = CreditFraction * MonthlyCommitCharge * BillingWindowWeight (daily weight = 1/#days_in_billing_period; weekly weight = 7/#days_in_billing_period). Credits are capped at 100% of the MonthlyCommitCharge for the affected window.
worked_examples: Example A (daily window): Customer commits 10,000 tokens/sec, daily billing window, MonthlyCommitCharge = $30,000. On March 5 the average observed throughput for the day = 8,000 tokens/sec (20% shortfall). CreditFraction = 0.20. Daily weight = 1/30 = 0.0333. CreditAmount = 0.20 * $30,000 * 0.0333 = $200. Net: $200 credit to apply to next invoice.

Example B (weekly window): Customer commits 50,000 tokens/sec, weekly billing window, MonthlyCommitCharge = $120,000. During the week the measured average drops to 45,000 tokens/sec (10% shortfall). Weekly weight = 7/30 = 0.2333. CreditAmount = 0.10 * $120,000 * 0.2333 = $2,800 (capped by monthly charge if above cap).
operational_playbook: Detection: Alert when 5-minute sliding average observed_throughput < 0.95 * committed_throughput for > 2 minutes. Alert channels: PagerDuty (oncall-runtime), Slack #dedicated-sla-incidents, Console incident panel.
Immediate mitigation: Runtime attempts fast-failover to warm spare pool if available. If autoscale policy is configured, attempt autoscale up to max burst within 60s and record capacity_event.

Customer notification: Automated email to customer's billing contact when crediting conditions are detected that will likely lead to a credit (includes preliminary observed shortfall and expected credit amount once computed at window end).

Escalation: If degradation continues > 1 hour, create postmortem stub and notify AM/TSM. For customers with P0 entitlement, open executive escalation and offer interim capacity temporarily at no extra cost while remediation is ongoing.

Credit issuance: At the end of the Billing Window, compute final CreditAmount. Legal/Billing system applies credit within two billing cycles and sends an official SLA credit notice. The Console exposes the calculation and raw metrics for audit.

Post-incident: Runtime to file RCA within 7 business days. Root cause categories must be tagged (hardware/power/network/software/third-party) and suggested remediation. Metrics and incident notes attached to the customer's SLA incident record.
open_questions: Should credits be pro-rated for partial refunds when customers have multi-tenant clusters and only a subset of workloads were impacted? (Proposed: credits apply at customer-level committed charge, not per-workload.)

How do we treat transient provider-region-wide events (cloud provider API/region outage)? Proposed: mark as exclusion if provider outage is confirmed and affects >50% of Redwood managed regional capacity that day.

Should we provide optional 'sustained-degradation' higher credit tiers for customers who experience repeated incidents in a 90-day rolling window? (Suggested: escalation clauses and potential contract re-rate after 3 incidents)
